Microsoft is considering using a Chinese AI model inside your office software — amplifying how your [AI](https://www.axios.com/technology/automation-and-ai) strategy is both a security and a cost calculation now.

**Why it matters:**Unlike closed models such as Anthropic's Claude or OpenAI's ChatGPT, open-source AI is free to download, cheaper to run, and dominated by [China](https://www.axios.com/world/china).

**Between the lines:**Microsoft [exploring a secured version](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTYvbWljcm9zb2Z0LWNvcGlsb3QtY293b3JrLXRva2VubWF4eGluZy1jb3dvcms_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cBae26b83c) of China-built DeepSeek V4 to power Copilot Cowork — its agentic assistant and the most compute-hungry part of Microsoft 365 — shows that even the richest software company on Earth can't hold the line on closed American-only models. You probably can't either.

**The security catch:**Microsoft's "secured" version would keep your data on its cloud platform Azure, not Chinese servers, which means the open-source question is shifting from *if* to*how.*

- But many vendors and tools don't offer that protection. That's why every CEO needs to be wary before approving any model.*(See next item.)*

**"Open source" means** the model weights — the actual trained intelligence — are public. Anyone can download, modify and deploy them. The best-performing, most-used ones are Chinese.

- DeepSeek V4 and other leading Chinese models are considered a few months behind frontier American models performance-wise. But [that gap is closing fast](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcmVuYS5haS9sZWFkZXJib2FyZC9hZ2VudD91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB7c1ce866) with buzzy new models like Z.ai's GLM 5.2.
- Smart CTOs and engineers are already handing off routine work to open-source models and saving pricier models for harder, more complex tasks.

**The part you may not see:** Many CEOs reading this are already running Chinese models somewhere in their stack and don't know it, because their vendors and engineers chose them on price.

**Worth watching:** Flo Crivello, CEO of AI agent platform Lindy, switched his company entirely to DeepSeek V4, citing millions in savings and better performance on core use cases — while keeping it on American soil, hosted by a U.S. provider rather than Chinese sources.

- Even so, the migration took months and far more engineering than expected.

**The bottom line:**Open-source Chinese models are good enough for most work at a fraction of the price. But you've got to be clear-eyed about their use.

## The Chinese way

Dominating open-source AI is China's national strategy.

**Why it matters:**Your company likely already faces thorny China-centric compliance questions — especially if you've staffed your tech team with AI enablers.

- Every open-source model your developers run from a Chinese lab ties part of your infrastructure to Beijing, whether you intended it or not.

**Between the lines:** The fear isn't just that Beijing has a potential backdoor into your company. It's the regulatory threat to your entire workflow as U.S.-China competition escalates.

- Bringing Chinese open-source models into the fold means you're using a product built by companies [legally required to cooperate](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGhzLmdvdi9zaXRlcy9kZWZhdWx0L2ZpbGVzL3B1YmxpY2F0aW9ucy8yMF8xMjIyX2RhdGEtc2VjdXJpdHktYnVzaW5lc3MtYWR2aXNvcnkucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cBb6aec6ce) with Chinese state intelligence.
- You can't be sure their future decisions won't be China-centric. They may propose ways to connect with their models that force a decision: Build for open source or tie to a frontier model.
- I'm not arguing against open source — just illuminating the reality we face.

**We've been here before:**Banning Huawei from the telecom networks of the U.S. and its closest allies cost billions to rip out and replace.

- Imagine the cost if companies across the West had to reconfigure their AI stacks overnight.

**Zoom out:**This isn't a fringe risk. Chinese companies — DeepSeek, Xiaomi, MiniMax, Tencent, Alibaba — [now dominate OpenRouter](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVucm91dGVyLmFpL3JhbmtpbmdzP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cCd1b730c5), the industry's most honest real-time scoreboard of developer usage, with DeepSeek at No. 1.

- The models you have to worry about are the same ones your team most wants to use.

**Worth noting:** Not all open models are Chinese. Meta's Llama and Europe's Mistral are credible alternatives with no ties to Beijing.

## 📋 A CEO checklist: All of us should ask and know ...

- **Which models are actually running in our stack?** Are our engineers and vendors routing to models beyond those we bought right now?
- **Where does our data physically go?**A model hosted on Azure or AWS keeps data in your cloud. A raw API call to a Chinese lab may not.
- **Who built it, and what law governs them?** Remember that Chinese labs are legally obligated to cooperate with state intelligence.
- **What breaks if we have to rip it out?**If regulation forces a switch, how deep is the dependency: a single feature or the foundation?
- **Are we choosing on price alone?** Lower token cost is a real advantage, but "it was cheaper" shouldn't be the whole answer if someone asks.

## America's competing interests

America made the opposite bet of China: We went all-in on our ahead-of-the-pack frontier proprietary models.

**The big picture:** The U.S. incentivized its frontier AI labs to optimize for revenue — with eyes on $1T+ IPOs. That pushed them toward subscriptions and closed ecosystems where every use can be metered.

**Meta was the major open exception**on American shores. Meta's 2023 release of Llama 2 was a breakthrough, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang later [called it](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9ibG9ncy5udmlkaWEuY29tL2Jsb2cvenVja2VyYmVyZy1odWFuZy8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB61db0c1f) "probably the biggest event in AI" from that year.

- But Meta's main business was already built around ads, allowing it to push for an open AI ecosystem it could shape.
- Then Meta got hit with a [huge cost](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.) of compute — and shifted its strategy away from the open ecosystem it once championed to play catch-up with Anthropic and OpenAI.
- Its newest model, [Muse Spark](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9hYm91dC5mYi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDI2LzA0L2ludHJvZHVjaW5nLW11c2Utc3BhcmstbWV0YS1zdXBlcmludGVsbGlnZW5jZS1sYWJzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB6d10344e), is closed-weight. And it's now testing [paid AI subscriptions](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8wNS8yNy9tZXRhLXRlc3RpbmctYWktc3Vic2NyaXB0aW9uLXNlcnZpY2VzLWNoZWFwZXN0LXBsYW4tYXQtN3BvaW50OTktYS1tb250aC5odG1sP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB18c672f3).

**The bottom line:** In the U.S., economics mean the AI feedback loop has to be mostly proprietary: Each lab learns from its own users, then sells the improvements back to them.

## The complicated counterattack

Open-source advocates think American frontier labs are begging for regulation in order to corner the AI market.

**Their claim:**Costly compliance requirements — think: safety audits or liability frameworks — would be trivial for companies like Anthropic or OpenAI and fatal to any open-source project.

- With enough regulation, the market would be forced to consolidate around the companies the government deems safe. Inevitably, that'd be the most powerful frontier labs.

**What they're saying:**Former White House AI czar David Sacks, who still [has President Trump's ear](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDUvMjEvdHJ1bXAtYWktZXhlY3V0aXZlLW9yZGVyLXBvc3Rwb25lZC13aHk_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB81e1be43) on cutting-edge issues, outlined this "regulatory capture agenda" on [last weekend's episode](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL2VwaXNvZGUvNmczSzRKZXFwZjFpbENkU1NMRTZhQT9zaT0yMTUzYmNjOGI0MTg0YmQyJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB62f3a735) of the "All-In" podcast.

- "You've got [Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei] who's out there describing these risks in a very hyperbolic way, and it's very clear where their agenda is headed, which is ... banning open-source models," Sacks said.
- "We're gonna be stuck with somewhere between one and three companies — maybe two — they'll be an AI monopoly or duopoly and they're gonna decide, along with some new government agency, which'll be a revolving door to their companies, who has access to what capabilities," he continued.

**Yes, but:**Sacks was bemoaning [the guardrails](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMDkvYW50aHJvcGljLW15dGhvcy1jbGFzcy1zYWZlZ3VhcmRzP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB7b59d260) Anthropic had established around discussing cybersecurity and biology with its powerful Fable model. But the episode was recorded *before* the Trump administration [issued export controls](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTIvYW50aHJvcGljLXRydW1wLW15dGhvcy1mYWJsZS1uYXRpb25hbC1zZWN1cml0eT91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB465d6140) that caused Anthropic to shut down consumer access to it.

- Anthropic has had [its share of spats](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDQvMjkvdHJ1bXAtYW50aHJvcGljLXBlbnRhZ29uLWFpLWV4ZWN1dGl2ZS1vcmRlci1nb3Y_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB5f0900f4) with the Trump White House. But the move is [a massive alarm bell](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTYvYWktYW50aHJvcGljLWV4cG9ydC1jb250cm9scz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cBa3f431e6) for the closed frontier labs themselves.
- They profit from having the best models, but now risk the government cutting off consumer access when that goal is achieved.

**The bottom line:**For the moment, the frontier labs are feeling the sting of government regulation long before any open-source model creators.

## The case for open source

*I asked Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO of Reflection AI, an American open frontier lab, to make the pro-open-source case to other CEOs.*

- Reflection, backed by Nvidia, [says it has](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9yZWZsZWN0aW9uLmFpL2Jsb2cvZnJvbnRpZXItb3Blbi1pbnRlbGxpZ2VuY2UvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cBa7e57a04) "identified a scalable commercial model that aligns with our open intelligence strategy."
- Demand is clearly there. Its valuation jumped from [$545M](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmxvb21iZXJnLmNvbS9uZXdzL2FydGljbGVzLzIwMjUtMDMtMDcvZXgtZGVlcG1pbmQtcmVzZWFyY2hlcnMtbmV3LXN0YXJ0dXAtYWltcy1mb3Itc3VwZXJpbnRlbGxpZ2VuY2U_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB05c2c83a) in March 2025 to [$8B](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.) in October 2025 to a potential [$25B](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.) in a March fundraising round. It hasn't yet released a model.

**Open models are a geopolitical priority.**They're Trojan horses for the infrastructure they bring with them. When a nation or enterprise adopts an open model, it also adopts the chips and software stack that come with it natively.

- **There is a sovereign market that closed models can't serve.**Enterprises that need full control over cost, security and deployment, and governments that must run AI on their own terms, require open models.
- **Renting vs. owning your intelligence.** Closed models only rent out AI capability, while open models give you ownership.
- **For CEOs, open source is a strategic advantage and control play.** You control cost, deployment, security and ultimately your own AI capabilities.

Worth watching: Flo Crivello, CEO of AI agent platform Lindy, switched his company entirely to DeepSeek V4, citing millions in savings and better performance on core use cases — while keeping it on American soil, hosted by a U.S. provider rather than Chinese sources.
Even so, the migration took months and far more engineering than expected.
The bottom line: Open-source Chinese models are good enough for most work at a fraction of the price. But you've got to be clear-eyed about their use.
Dominating open-source AI is China's national strategy.
Why it matters: Your company likely already faces thorny China-centric compliance questions — especially if you've staffed your tech team with AI enablers.
Every open-source model your developers run from a Chinese lab ties part of your infrastructure to Beijing, whether you intended it or not.
Between the lines: The fear isn't just that Beijing has a potential backdoor into your company. It's the regulatory threat to your entire workflow as U.S.-China competition escalates.
Bringing Chinese open-source models into the fold means you're using a product built by companies legally required to cooperate with Chinese state intelligence.
You can't be sure their future decisions won't be China-centric. They may propose ways to connect with their models that force a decision: Build for open source or tie to a frontier model.
I'm not arguing against open source — just illuminating the reality we face.
We've been here before: Banning Huawei from the telecom networks of the U.S. and its closest allies cost billions to rip out and replace.
Imagine the cost if companies across the West had to reconfigure their AI stacks overnight.
Zoom out: This isn't a fringe risk. Chinese companies — DeepSeek, Xiaomi, MiniMax, Tencent, Alibaba — now dominate OpenRouter , the industry's most honest real-time scoreboard of developer usage, with DeepSeek at No. 1.
The models you have to worry about are the same ones your team most wants to use.
Worth noting: Not all open models are Chinese. Meta's Llama and Europe's Mistral are credible alternatives with no ties to Beijing.
📋 A CEO checklist: All of us should ask and know ...
Which models are actually running in our stack? Are our engineers and vendors routing to models beyond those we bought right now?
Where does our data physically go? A model hosted on Azure or AWS keeps data in your cloud. A raw API call to a Chinese lab may not.
Who built it, and what law governs them? Remember that Chinese labs are legally obligated to cooperate with state intelligence.
What breaks if we have to rip it out? If regulation forces a switch, how deep is the dependency: a single feature or the foundation?
Are we choosing on price alone? Lower token cost is a real advantage, but "it was cheaper" shouldn't be the whole answer if someone asks.
America's competing interests
America made the opposite bet of China: We went all-in on our ahead-of-the-pack frontier proprietary models.
The big picture: The U.S. incentivized its frontier AI labs to optimize for revenue — with eyes on $1T+ IPOs. That pushed them toward subscriptions and closed ecosystems where every use can be metered.
Meta was the major open exception on American shores. Meta's 2023 release of Llama 2 was a breakthrough, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang later called it "probably the biggest event in AI" from that year.
But Meta's main business was already built around ads, allowing it to push for an open AI ecosystem it could shape.
Then Meta got hit with a huge cost of compute — and shifted its strategy away from the open ecosystem it once championed to play catch-up with Anthropic and OpenAI.
Its newest model, Muse Spark , is closed-weight. And it's now testing paid AI subscriptions .
The bottom line: In the U.S., economics mean the AI feedback loop has to be mostly proprietary: Each lab learns from its own users, then sells the improvements back to them.
The complicated counterattack
Open-source advocates think American frontier labs are begging for regulation in order to corner the AI market.
Their claim: Costly compliance requirements — think: safety audits or liability frameworks — would be trivial for companies like Anthropic or OpenAI and fatal to any open-source project.
With enough regulation, the market would be forced to consolidate around the companies the government deems safe. Inevitably, that'd be the most powerful frontier labs.
What they're saying: Former White House AI czar David Sacks, who still has President Trump's ear on cutting-edge issues, outlined this "regulatory capture agenda" on last weekend's episode of the "All-In" podcast.
"You've got [Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei] who's out there describing these risks in a very hyperbolic way, and it's very clear where their agenda is headed, which is ... banning open-source models," Sacks said.
"We're gonna be stuck with somewhere between one and three companies — maybe two — they'll be an AI monopoly or duopoly and they're gonna decide, along with some new government agency, which'll be a revolving door to their companies, who has access to what capabilities," he continued.
Yes, but: Sacks was bemoaning the guardrails Anthropic had established around discussing cybersecurity and biology with its powerful Fable model. But the episode was recorded before the Trump administration issued export controls that caused Anthropic to shut down consumer access to it.
Anthropic has had its share of spats with the Trump White House. But the move is a massive alarm bell for the closed frontier labs themselves.
They profit from having the best models, but now risk the government cutting off consumer access when that goal is achieved.
The bottom line: For the moment, the frontier labs are feeling the sting of government regulation long before any open-source model creators.
I asked Misha Laskin, co-founder and CEO of Reflection AI, an American open frontier lab, to make the pro-open-source case to other CEOs.
Reflection, backed by Nvidia, says it has "identified a scalable commercial model that aligns with our open intelligence strategy."
Demand is clearly there. Its valuation jumped from $545M in March 2025 to $8B in October 2025 to a potential $25B in a March fundraising round. It hasn't yet released a model.
Open models are a geopolitical priority. They're Trojan horses for the infrastructure they bring with them. When a nation or enterprise adopts an open model, it also adopts the chips and software stack that come with it natively.
There is a sovereign market that closed models can't serve. Enterprises that need full control over cost, security and deployment, and governments that must run AI on their own terms, require open models.
Renting vs. owning your intelligence. Closed models only rent out AI capability, while open models give you ownership.
For CEOs, open source is a strategic advantage and control play. You control cost, deployment, security and ultimately your own AI capabilities.

微軟正考慮在你的辦公軟體中使用中國 AI 模型，這凸顯了現在你的 [AI](https://www.axios.com/technology/automation-and-ai) 策略同時也是安全與成本的考量。

**為什麼重要：** 不同於 Anthropic 的 Claude 或 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 這類封閉模型，開源 AI 可以免費下載、運行成本較低，而且由[中國](https://www.axios.com/world/china)主導。

**弦外之音：**Microsoft [正在探索中國打造的 DeepSeek V4 安全版](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTYvbWljcm9zb2Z0LWNvcGlsb3QtY293b3JrLXRva2VubWF4eGluZy1jb3dvcms_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cBae26b83c)，用來支撐 Copilot Cowork，也就是它的代理型助理，以及 Microsoft 365 裡最吃算力的部分。這顯示，就連地表最有錢的軟體公司，也無法堅守只用封閉、純美國模型的防線。你大概也不行。

**安全上的但書：**Microsoft 所謂的「安全版」會把你的資料留在它的雲端平台 Azure，而不是中國伺服器上。這代表開源問題正在從*是否*使用，轉向*如何*使用。

- 但許多供應商和工具並不提供這層保護。這就是為什麼每位 CEO 在核准任何模型前都需要保持警覺。*（見下一項。）*

**「開源」指的是**模型權重，也就是實際訓練出的智慧，是公開的。任何人都可以下載、修改和部署。表現最好、使用最廣的開源模型，多半來自中國。

- 就效能來看，DeepSeek V4 和其他領先的中國模型，被認為仍落後美國前沿模型幾個月。但隨著 Z.ai 的 GLM 5.2 這類備受矚目的新模型出現，[這個差距正在快速縮小](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9hcmVuYS5haS9sZWFkZXJib2FyZC9hZ2VudD91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB7c1ce866)。
- 聰明的 CTO 和工程師已經把例行工作交給開源模型，把更昂貴的模型留給更困難、更複雜的任務。

**你可能沒看到的部分：**許多讀到這裡的 CEO，其實已經在自家技術堆疊的某處跑著中國模型，而且自己並不知道，因為他們的供應商和工程師是基於價格選了這些模型。

**值得關注：**AI 代理平台 Lindy 的 CEO Flo Crivello 已經把公司全面切換到 DeepSeek V4，理由是省下數百萬美元，且在核心使用情境上表現更好；同時仍把模型留在美國境內，由美國供應商託管，而不是來自中國的服務。

- 即便如此，這場遷移仍花了數月時間，所需工程投入也遠比預期多。

**重點是：**中國開源模型已經好到足以應付大多數工作，而且價格只是零頭。但你必須清楚看待它們的使用風險。

## 中國路線

主導開源 AI 是中國的國家戰略。

**為什麼重要：**你的公司很可能已經面臨棘手的中國相關合規問題，尤其是如果你的技術團隊已經配置了推動 AI 導入的人才。

- 你的開發者每跑一個來自中國實驗室的開源模型，就等於把你基礎設施的一部分和北京綁在一起，不管你原本是不是這樣打算。

**弦外之音：**令人擔心的不只是北京可能在你的公司裡留有後門，而是隨著美中競爭升高，你整套工作流程都可能面臨監管威脅。

- 把中國開源模型納入體系，代表你正在使用由[依法必須配合](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZGhzLmdvdi9zaXRlcy9kZWZhdWx0L2ZpbGVzL3B1YmxpY2F0aW9ucy8yMF8xMjIyX2RhdGEtc2VjdXJpdHktYnVzaW5lc3MtYWR2aXNvcnkucGRmP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cBb6aec6ce)中國國家情報機關的公司所打造的產品。
- 你無法確定它們未來的決策不會以中國為中心。它們可能提出與其模型連接的方式，迫使你做出選擇：為開源而建，或是綁定某個前沿模型。
- 我不是在反對開源，只是在說明我們面對的現實。

**我們以前遇過類似情況：**禁止華為進入美國及其最親近盟友的電信網路，最後花了數十億美元才完成拆除與替換。

- 想像一下，如果西方各地的公司必須一夜之間重新配置自己的 AI 技術堆疊，成本會有多高。

**拉遠來看：**這不是邊緣風險。中國公司，包括 DeepSeek、小米、MiniMax、騰訊、阿里巴巴，如今已經[主導 OpenRouter](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVucm91dGVyLmFpL3JhbmtpbmdzP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cCd1b730c5)。這是業界最誠實反映開發者使用情況的即時排行榜，其中 DeepSeek 排名第一。

- 你必須擔心的那些模型，正是你的團隊最想使用的模型。

**值得注意：**並非所有開源模型都來自中國。Meta 的 Llama 和歐洲的 Mistral 都是可信的替代選項，而且與北京沒有關聯。

## 📋 CEO 檢查清單：我們都應該問清楚、也該知道……

- **我們的技術堆疊裡實際上跑的是哪些模型？** 我們的工程師和供應商，現在是否把請求導向我們採購範圍之外的模型？
- **我們的資料實際上會被送到哪裡？**部署在 Azure 或 AWS 上的模型，會把資料留在你的雲端環境裡。直接呼叫中國實驗室的原始 API，則未必如此。
- **誰打造了它？適用哪一國法律？** 別忘了，中國實驗室依法有義務配合國家情報機關。
- **如果我們必須把它抽換掉，會壞在哪裡？**如果法規迫使我們切換，依賴程度有多深：只是單一功能，還是整個基礎架構？
- **我們是否只看價格在做選擇？** 較低的 token 成本確實是優勢，但如果有人追問，「因為比較便宜」不該是唯一答案。

## 美國的利益拉扯

美國押下了與中國相反的賭注：我們全力投入領先群雄的前沿專有模型。

**大局來看：** 美國鼓勵自家的前沿 AI 實驗室以營收為優化目標，眼睛盯著 1 兆美元以上的 IPO。這推動它們走向訂閱制與封閉生態系，讓每一次使用都可以被計量收費。

**Meta 是美國本土主要的開放例外。**Meta 在 2023 年發布 Llama 2 是一項突破，Nvidia 執行長黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）後來[稱它](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9ibG9ncy5udmlkaWEuY29tL2Jsb2cvenVja2VyYmVyZy1odWFuZy8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB61db0c1f)是那一年「可能是 AI 領域最大的事件」。

- 但 Meta 的主要業務本來就已經建立在廣告之上，讓它得以推動一個由自己塑造的開放 AI 生態系。
- 接著 Meta 被運算的[龐大成本](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.)重擊，並把策略從它曾經力挺的開放生態系，轉向追趕 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。
- 它最新的模型 [Muse Spark](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9hYm91dC5mYi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDI2LzA0L2ludHJvZHVjaW5nLW11c2Utc3BhcmstbWV0YS1zdXBlcmludGVsbGlnZW5jZS1sYWJzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB6d10344e) 是封閉權重。而且它現在也在測試[付費 AI 訂閱](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8wNS8yNy9tZXRhLXRlc3RpbmctYWktc3Vic2NyaXB0aW9uLXNlcnZpY2VzLWNoZWFwZXN0LXBsYW4tYXQtN3BvaW50OTktYS1tb250aC5odG1sP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB18c672f3)。

**重點是：**在美國，經濟邏輯意味著 AI 的回饋循環大多必須是專有的：每個實驗室從自己的使用者身上學習，再把改進後的成果賣回給他們。

## 複雜的反擊

開源倡議者認為，美國的前沿 AI 實驗室是在乞求監管，好壟斷 AI 市場。

**他們的主張：**昂貴的合規要求，例如安全稽核或責任框架，對 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 這類公司來說微不足道，卻足以讓任何開源專案致命。

- 只要監管夠多，市場就會被迫整併到政府認定安全的公司周圍。不可避免地，那會是最強大的前沿實驗室。

## 開源的理由

*我請美國開放式前沿實驗室 Reflection AI 共同創辦人暨執行長 Misha Laskin，向其他 CEO 說明支持開源的論點。*

**開放模型是地緣政治上的優先事項。**它們像特洛伊木馬，會把背後的基礎設施一起帶進來。當一個國家或企業採用開放模型，也會一併採用原生搭配的晶片與軟體堆疊。

- **有一個封閉模型無法服務的主權市場。**需要完全掌控成本、安全與部署的企業，以及必須按照自身條件運行 AI 的政府，都需要開放模型。

- **租用你的智慧，還是擁有你的智慧。**封閉模型只是出租 AI 能力，開放模型則讓你取得所有權。

- **對執行長而言，開源是一種戰略優勢，也是一種掌控權。**你能掌控成本、部署、安全，最終也能掌控自己的 AI 能力。

## 中國路線

主導開源 AI 是中國的國家戰略。

**為什麼重要：**你的公司很可能已經面臨棘手的中國相關合規問題，尤其是如果你的技術團隊已經配置了推動 AI 導入的人才。

- 你的開發者每跑一個來自中國實驗室的開源模型，就等於把你基礎設施的一部分和北京綁在一起，不管你原本是不是這樣打算。

**弦外之音：**令人擔心的不只是北京可能在你的公司裡留有後門，而是隨著美中競爭升高，你整套工作流程都可能面臨監管威脅。

- 你無法確定它們未來的決策不會以中國為中心。它們可能提出與其模型連接的方式，迫使你做出選擇：為開源而建，或是綁定某個前沿模型。
- 我不是在反對開源，只是在說明我們面對的現實。

**我們以前遇過類似情況：**禁止華為進入美國及其最親近盟友的電信網路，最後花了數十億美元才完成拆除與替換。

- 想像一下，如果西方各地的公司必須一夜之間重新配置自己的 AI 技術堆疊，成本會有多高。

**拉遠來看：**這不是邊緣風險。中國公司，包括 DeepSeek、小米、MiniMax、騰訊、阿里巴巴，如今已經[主導 OpenRouter](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVucm91dGVyLmFpL3JhbmtpbmdzP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cCd1b730c5)。這是業界最誠實反映開發者使用情況的即時排行榜，其中 DeepSeek 排名第一。

**值得注意：**並非所有開源模型都來自中國。Meta 的 Llama 和歐洲的 Mistral 都是可信的替代選項，而且與北京沒有關聯。

- **誰打造了它？適用哪一國法律？** 別忘了，中國實驗室依法有義務配合國家情報機關。

- **我們是否只看價格在做選擇？** 較低的 token 成本確實是優勢，但如果有人追問，「因為比較便宜」不該是唯一答案。

## 美國的利益拉扯

美國押下了與中國相反的賭注：我們全力投入領先群雄的前沿專有模型。

**大局來看：** 美國鼓勵自家的前沿 AI 實驗室以營收為優化目標，眼睛盯著 1 兆美元以上的 IPO。這推動它們走向訂閱制與封閉生態系，讓每一次使用都可以被計量收費。

**Meta 是美國本土主要的開放例外。**Meta 在 2023 年發布 Llama 2 是一項突破，Nvidia 執行長黃仁勳（Jensen Huang）後來[稱它](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9ibG9ncy5udmlkaWEuY29tL2Jsb2cvenVja2VyYmVyZy1odWFuZy8_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB61db0c1f)是那一年「可能是 AI 領域最大的事件」。

- 但 Meta 的主要業務本來就已經建立在廣告之上，讓它得以推動一個由自己塑造的開放 AI 生態系。
- 接著 Meta 被運算的[龐大成本](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.)重擊，並把策略從它曾經力挺的開放生態系，轉向追趕 Anthropic 和 OpenAI。
- 它最新的模型 [Muse Spark](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9hYm91dC5mYi5jb20vbmV3cy8yMDI2LzA0L2ludHJvZHVjaW5nLW11c2Utc3BhcmstbWV0YS1zdXBlcmludGVsbGlnZW5jZS1sYWJzLz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB6d10344e) 是封閉權重。而且它現在也在測試[付費 AI 訂閱](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuY25iYy5jb20vMjAyNi8wNS8yNy9tZXRhLXRlc3RpbmctYWktc3Vic2NyaXB0aW9uLXNlcnZpY2VzLWNoZWFwZXN0LXBsYW4tYXQtN3BvaW50OTktYS1tb250aC5odG1sP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB18c672f3)。

**重點是：**在美國，經濟邏輯意味著 AI 的回饋循環大多必須是專有的：每個實驗室從自己的使用者身上學習，再把改進後的成果賣回給他們。

## 複雜的反擊

開源倡議者認為，美國的前沿 AI 實驗室是在乞求監管，好壟斷 AI 市場。

**他們的主張：**昂貴的合規要求，例如安全稽核或責任框架，對 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 這類公司來說微不足道，卻足以讓任何開源專案致命。

- 只要監管夠多，市場就會被迫整併到政府認定安全的公司周圍。不可避免地，那會是最強大的前沿實驗室。

**他們怎麼說：**前白宮 AI 主管 David Sacks 在前沿議題上仍[能影響川普總統](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDUvMjEvdHJ1bXAtYWktZXhlY3V0aXZlLW9yZGVyLXBvc3Rwb25lZC13aHk_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB81e1be43)，他在上週末「All-In」Podcast 的[節目](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnNwb3RpZnkuY29tL2VwaXNvZGUvNmczSzRKZXFwZjFpbENkU1NMRTZhQT9zaT0yMTUzYmNjOGI0MTg0YmQyJnV0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB62f3a735)中，概述了這套「監管俘虜議程」。

- Sacks 說：「你看到 [Anthropic 執行長 Dario Amodei] 在外面用非常誇張的方式描述這些風險，而且他們的議程要往哪裡走已經非常清楚，也就是……禁止開源模型。」
- 他接著說：「我們會卡在一到三家公司之間，也許是兩家；它們會形成 AI 壟斷或雙頭壟斷，然後它們會和某個新的政府機構一起決定誰能取得哪些能力，而那個機構會成為通往這些公司的旋轉門。」

**沒錯，不過：**Sacks 當時是在抱怨 Anthropic 圍繞其強大的 Fable 模型討論網路安全與生物學時所設下的[護欄](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMDkvYW50aHJvcGljLW15dGhvcy1jbGFzcy1zYWZlZ3VhcmRzP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB7b59d260)。但這集節目是在川普政府[發布出口管制](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTIvYW50aHJvcGljLXRydW1wLW15dGhvcy1mYWJsZS1uYXRpb25hbC1zZWN1cml0eT91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cB465d6140)之前錄製的；這項管制造成 Anthropic 關閉一般消費者對該模型的存取。

- Anthropic 和川普白宮之間也曾有[一些摩擦](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDQvMjkvdHJ1bXAtYW50aHJvcGljLXBlbnRhZ29uLWFpLWV4ZWN1dGl2ZS1vcmRlci1nb3Y_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB5f0900f4)。但這項舉動對封閉式前沿實驗室本身來說，是[巨大的警訊](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYXhpb3MuY29tLzIwMjYvMDYvMTYvYWktYW50aHJvcGljLWV4cG9ydC1jb250cm9scz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249bmV3c2xldHRlcl9jc3VpdGVfYmV0YSZzdHJlYW09dG9w/586d9e571e560373298b467cBa3f431e6)。

**重點是：**目前，前沿實驗室比任何開源模型創作者都更早感受到政府監管帶來的刺痛。

## 開源的理由

*我請美國開放式前沿實驗室 Reflection AI 共同創辦人暨執行長 Misha Laskin，向其他 CEO 說明支持開源的論點。*

- 獲 Nvidia 支持的 Reflection [表示它已](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly9yZWZsZWN0aW9uLmFpL2Jsb2cvZnJvbnRpZXItb3Blbi1pbnRlbGxpZ2VuY2UvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9bmV3c2xldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cBa7e57a04)「找到一套可擴展的商業模式，並且符合我們的開放智慧策略。」
- 需求顯然存在。它的估值從 2025 年 3 月的 [5.45 億美元](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmxvb21iZXJnLmNvbS9uZXdzL2FydGljbGVzLzIwMjUtMDMtMDcvZXgtZGVlcG1pbmQtcmVzZWFyY2hlcnMtbmV3LXN0YXJ0dXAtYWltcy1mb3Itc3VwZXJpbnRlbGxpZ2VuY2U_dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1uZXdzbGV0dGVyJnV0bV9tZWRpdW09ZW1haWwmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPW5ld3NsZXR0ZXJfY3N1aXRlX2JldGEmc3RyZWFtPXRvcA/586d9e571e560373298b467cB05c2c83a)，一路跳升到 2025 年 10 月的 [80 億美元](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.1626/aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI1LzEwLzA5L3JlZmxlY3Rpb24tcmFpc2VzLTJiLXRvLWJlLWFtZXJpY2FzLW9wZW4tZnJvbnRpZXItYWktbGFiLWNoYWxsZW5naW5nLWRlZXBzZWVrLz91dG1fc291cmNlPW5ldHRlciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1uZXdzbGV0dGVyX2NzdWl0ZV9iZXRhJnN0cmVhbT10b3A/586d9e571e560373298b467cB810fe6d0)，並可能在 3 月的一輪募資中達到 [250 億美元](https://link.axios.com/click/46236832.)。它目前尚未發布模型。

**開放模型是地緣政治上的優先事項。**它們像特洛伊木馬，會把背後的基礎設施一起帶進來。當一個國家或企業採用開放模型，也會一併採用原生搭配的晶片與軟體堆疊。

- **有一個封閉模型無法服務的主權市場。**需要完全掌控成本、安全與部署的企業，以及必須按照自身條件運行 AI 的政府，都需要開放模型。

- **租用你的智慧，還是擁有你的智慧。**封閉模型只是出租 AI 能力，開放模型則讓你取得所有權。

- **對執行長而言，開源是一種戰略優勢，也是一種掌控權。**你能掌控成本、部署、安全，最終也能掌控自己的 AI 能力。
